title: Daily routines
subtitle: wake up, have a snack, do the ironing, eat out, come round
summary: Describe your day from waking up to going out, using the right verbs with sleep, food, the bathroom and housework.

lesson.heading: Sleep
lesson.text: You **wake up** (= stop sleeping) and then **get up** (= get out of bed) a few minutes later. In the evening you **go to bed**, and then **go to sleep** (also **fall asleep**). **Straight away** means immediately.

examples.text: During the week I usually **wake up** about 7.30 am. If I don't, my mum **wakes** me **up**.
I **go to bed** about 10.30 pm, and usually **go to sleep straight away**.
If I have a **late night**, I try to **have a sleep** in the afternoon.
examples.note: a late night = you go to bed very late; the opposite is an early night. Have a sleep = sleep for a short time, e.g. half an hour

lesson.heading: Food
lesson.text: A **light lunch** is a small meal. A **snack** is a small amount of food between meals. Your **main meal** is the biggest one of the day. If you don't **bother** to do something, you don't do it because there is no reason or it is too much work. A **takeaway** is a meal you buy in a restaurant but eat at home.

examples.text: I have coffee and **cereal** for breakfast, then a **light lunch** and a **snack** in the afternoon.
We have our **main meal** in the evening.
If Mum's late home from work, she doesn't **bother** to cook; we just get a **takeaway** instead.
One of us has to **feed** the cat as well.

lesson.heading: Bathroom routines
lesson.text: You **have a shower**, **have a bath** or just **have a wash**. You **clean your teeth** (also **brush your teeth**). Men **have a shave**, and some people **put on make-up**. **Instead of** means in place of.

examples.text: I only have time to **have a wash** and **clean my teeth**.
Rosie comes in to **put on** a bit of **make-up**.
In the winter I sometimes **have a bath instead of** a shower.
Marcus is **having a shave** in the bathroom.

lesson.heading: Housework
lesson.text: **Housework** is the work of keeping a home clean and tidy. A **cleaner** is a person you pay to clean. **Fortunately** (also **luckily**) means something happens because of good luck.

examples.text: **Fortunately** we've got a **cleaner** who does a lot of the **housework**.
I still have to **make my bed** and do some of my **ironing**.
I sometimes **do the shopping** with Mum.

lesson.heading: do the shopping and go shopping

left.label: do the shopping
left.text: You buy food, usually at the supermarket. It is a job you have to do.
examples: I **do the shopping** on Saturday morning.
Could you **do the shopping** for me today?

right.label: go shopping
right.text: It is a leisure activity. You perhaps buy clothes, DVDs or books.
examples: We **went shopping** and I bought two new jackets.
I love **going shopping** with my sister.

lesson.heading: Spare time
lesson.text: **Spare time** is time when you are not working. You can **stay in** (= stay at home) or **go out**. **Eat out** means eat in a restaurant; the opposite is **eat in**. If friends **come round**, they visit you in your home, and you **chat** (= have an informal conversation).

examples.text: On weekdays I usually **stay in** and watch TV in the evening.
At the weekend I **go out** quite a lot with my friends, and I **eat out** once a week.
Sometimes friends **come round** and we **chat** about clothes, music and college.

lesson.heading: have + noun and do + noun
rows: have a late night / an early night

lesson.text: Go to bed is the moment you get into bed; go to sleep is the moment you start sleeping. You can go to bed at ten and not go to sleep until midnight.

exercises.prompt: Match the words on the left with the words on the right.
Do we use have or do with each of these?
My mother usually ___ me up around 7.30, then I get up about 7.45.
exercises.explanation: Wake somebody up = make them stop sleeping.

exercises.prompt: If I have a ___ in the afternoon, I usually eat fruit instead of chocolate.
exercises.hint: (a small amount of food between meals)
exercises.explanation: A snack is a small amount of food you eat between meals.

exercises.prompt: Does it cost much to have a cleaner to ___ the housework?
exercises.explanation: We say do the housework, do the washing, do the ironing.

exercises.prompt: Sometimes friends ___ round to the flat and we play computer games.
exercises.explanation: If friends come round, they visit you in your home.

exercises.prompt: I eat ___ at the weekend, usually in a local Italian or French restaurant.
exercises.explanation: Eat out = eat in a restaurant. The opposite is eat in.

exercises.prompt: I don't ___ with a full meal at lunchtime; I usually just have a light lunch, like a salad.
exercises.explanation: Not bother with something = not do it, because it is too much work.

exercises.prompt: I often have ___ for breakfast - usually cornflakes or something like that.
exercises.explanation: Cornflakes are a kind of cereal, a common breakfast food.

exercises.prompt: When I get emails, I try to reply to them straight ___.
*A:* Don't bother to cook tonight. We could go out ___ of eating here.
*B:* I'm tired, so I'd rather stay in. You don't have to cook - we can order a ___.
exercises.explanation: A takeaway is a meal you buy in a restaurant but eat at home.

exercises.statement: If you have a late night, you go to bed very early.
exercises.explanation: If you have a late night, you go to bed very late. The opposite is have an early night.
